items.titleRaw: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models
items.contentRaw: Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) achieve remarkable success on diverse multimodal understanding and generation tasks, yet they still struggle to effectively leverage language-based chain-of-thought reasoning for image generation. As a result, existing reasoning-augmented UMMs often fail to inherit the test-time scaling and fine-grained controllability observed in large language models. We attribute this failure to a fundamental modality mismatch: reasoning is performed in a discrete token space, whereas image generation operates in a continuous space. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Latent Reasoning framework in Continuous space (LARC), which alleviates the token-level bottleneck by reasoning over continuous hidden states. Specifically, the training framework consists of two stages: (i) curriculum supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and (ii) information-gain reinforcement learning (RL). First, the curriculum SFT stage gradually converts token-level reasoning into latent reasoning. Subsequently, the information-gain RL stage self-evolves latent reasoning without ground truth supervision. Experiments across diverse text-to-image generation benchmarks show that LARC consistently improves generation quality, prompt following, and compositional fidelity. Notably, LARC achieves state-of-the-art performance on GenEval with a 7%p gain over BAGEL and demonstrates clear test-time scaling behavior, outperforming token-based generation under both parallel and sequential test-time scaling strategies.

payloadJson.title: Latent Reasoning in Continuous Space for Unified Multimodal Models

items.titleRaw: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
items.contentRaw: Decision models such as Jev have emerged as a highly promising paradigm for LLM agent systems, providing lightweight and reliable categorical reasoning for rapid System One execution. However, existing generation-oriented inference engines fail to support these workloads effectively, suffering from severe prefix recomputation overheads or distorted output probabilities. To address this challenge, we propose Flide, an efficient and exact inference engine that decouples the logical tree structure of a decision request from its physical execution within a single flattened token stream. Through ForkAttention, Flide navigates request dependencies using GPU-resident indices across both standard attention and recurrent Gated DeltaNet layers, guaranteeing in exact arithmetic that every query branch evaluates identically to an isolated forward pass. By expressing branch topologies directly in GPU-resident metadata, Flide accommodates diverse request mixtures with a compact set of pre-recorded execution graphs while enabling expanding agent histories to resume from checkpoints saved in earlier passes. Extensive evaluations on public hybrid and decision models demonstrate that Flide answers queries up to 9.5 times faster than vLLM and SGLang while staying closest to a float32 reference in total variation distance. By unifying physical execution throughput with mathematical exactness, Flide establishes a principled foundation for scalable, latency-critical decision intelligence in agent systems.

payloadJson.title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking

items.titleRaw: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
items.contentRaw: Agentic workflows are increasingly shifting towards long-horizon tasks, such as open-ended scientific work, where models benefit from long context windows. However, at ultra-long context (above 1M tokens), full attention is prohibitively expensive. A promising approach is sparse attention, in which a dedicated indexer selects a subset of keys for the attention. Yet current methods of indexing either still have quadratic cost in context size or lose accuracy at ultra-long context scale. We address this with Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), an efficient attention method that maintains accuracy at ultra-long context. In LSA, keys are hierarchically clustered in a learned latent space, and queries score the hierarchy of clusters instead of scoring every key, making prefill, decode and training faster at long context. We propose two variants, Distilled-LSA (D-LSA), which can be applied to pre-trained models via distillation, and Native-LSA (N-LSA), which is trained natively on the next-token loss alone. On GLM-5.3-FLASH (QWEN-3.8-27B) at 10M tokens, D-LSA speeds up one attention layer by 22.7x (72.4x) in prefill and 4.6x (42.5x) in decode over its original sparse attention (full attention), while keeping similar accuracy across a variety of tasks. N-LSA matches the accuracy of full attention with a training speedup of 1.6x per layer at 128k tokens. LSA offers practical and efficient attention for models to benefit from ultra-long context.

payloadJson.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention

items.titleRaw: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
items.contentRaw: Planning with world models enables test-time adaptation for embodied agents, offering superior generalization over direct policy learning. However, long-horizon tasks remain hindered by cumulative errors and search complexity. Existing hierarchical methods often use rigid macro-actions or latent skills, leading to brittle representations and limited fine-grained control. We introduce ID-WM (Implicit Dynamics World Models), a hierarchical world model that decouples state-space reachability from local control. Our framework utilizes a high-level model to sample feasible transitions across the state manifold and a low-level world model as an inverse dynamics solver to ground these transitions into precise actions. This allows the planner to identify reachable subgoals without being constrained by low-level execution details. By prioritizing local physical feasibility over global behavioral patterns, ID-WM synthesizes novel long-horizon plans from short segments, transcending the specific behavioral modes seen during training. We demonstrate its effectiveness across three navigation and manipulation suites, achieving a 38.5% improvement over state-of-the-art policy and diffusion-based planners. Crucially, by leveraging this hierarchical structure to mitigate compounding errors, our approach yields a 135% performance gain over single-level world model MPC, particularly in complex, unseen configurations for long-horizon tasks. Videos can be viewed at https://id-wm.github.io

items.titleRaw: RoboArchitect: Automating the Design of Robotic Agents with Persistent Memory
items.contentRaw: Recent work shows that a frozen robot policy performs far better inside an agent harness, where control code decides when to query the policy, consult vision tools, or command the arm directly. Yet today these harnesses are built by hand and redesigned for each new robot or benchmark. We show that harness design can be automated, offering a strong alternative to finetuning on a novel setup. In RoboArchitect, a coding model observes a robot's rollouts, diagnoses failures, and iteratively revises the harness around the frozen policy. The harness evolves on a set of episodes for its optimization and is evaluated on held-out scenes and tasks. Without updating any model weights, RoboArchitect raises average success from 9.7% to 43.3% on unseen scenes (4.5x) and from 12.7% to 40.2% on unseen tasks (3.2x), across multiple benchmarks and policies. The gains are largest where the benchmark is far from the policy's training data: wrapping a general-purpose policy, the evolved harness yields a specialist that often outperforms even the finetuned version. Intuitive control strategies are automatically designed, such as lifting a jammed arm clear or reaching in horizontally when an obstacle blocks the way from above. The harness also evolves its own persistent memory, carrying learned experience, such as effective grasp depths, into later decisions. These results suggest that substantial headroom in robotic manipulation lies in the agent harness, and its design can be effectively automated and optimized without weight updates.

items.titleRaw: Counting on Dummies: Privacy Amplification with Observable Counts and Truncated Batches
items.contentRaw: In many practical deployments of Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD), the server processes data in batches. Randomly sampling these batches allows for better privacy bounds via privacy amplification results. Most sampling schemes with provable privacy amplification, including Poisson sampling and random allocation, result in variable batch sizes. The privacy guarantee of these schemes requires that the batch sizes are not revealed. In distributed settings, the server performing the aggregation or any party observing the communication traffic may learn these batch sizes. Furthermore, in both centralized and distributed settings, memory and computation constraints may require each batch to be of some maximum size $s$, necessitating truncation of the batch when it exceeds this limit. It is known that this truncation can result in a significant increase in privacy loss. In this work, we address both of these challenges via a simple mechanism that uses a random number of \emph{dummy points} to privatize the batch size and maintain the privacy guarantee even under truncation. We demonstrate that our mechanism is easy to implement in a distributed setting, and provide a general analysis of this mechanism for both Poisson sampling and random allocation. Our analysis is designed to support efficient and relatively tight privacy accounting. It also effectively amplifies the privacy of the count releases by subsampling, making the expected number of dummy points asymptotically smaller than what is needed to directly privatize the (sensitivity-one) batch sizes with non-negative noise. For Poisson sampling with truncated batches, we demonstrate empirically that our mechanism achieves better privacy--efficiency tradeoffs than the direct accounting for truncation recently given by (Ganesh, 2025).

payloadJson.title: Counting on Dummies: Privacy Amplification with Observable Counts and Truncated Batches

items.titleRaw: anthropics/claude-code v2.1.316 released
items.contentRaw:
## What's changed

- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK`, which turns the `ultrathink` keyword off
- Added pooled group budgets to the Claude apps gateway: one monthly budget that a group's members share, on top of each member's own limit, set with `pooled_budget` on the spend limits admin API
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_LOOPED_CROSS_CERT_DROP` to keep system cross-certificates that certify each other in a loop, for servers whose private CA needs one
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT` to set the effort level subagents run at when nothing else names one, instead of inheriting the session's
- Added `managed.policy_mode: layered` to the Claude apps gateway: every policy that matches a developer applies, each merged over the ones listed below it, not only the first
- Added `guardrail.input_tagging` on Claude apps gateway Bedrock upstreams, which wraps prompts in the input tags that an Amazon Bedrock guardrail's prompt attacks filter needs; `all_messages_and_system` also tags the system prompt
- Deprecated fast mode for Opus 4.8 as of October 30, 2026; it will be removed on November 30, 2026. After removal, fast mode requests on Opus 4.8 return an error and do not fall back to standard Opus 4.8. Migrate to Opus 5.5 to keep the speedup
- Fixed shell commands being left running on macOS and Linux when Claude Code exits by itself, for example when credentials are refused or a cloud session is archived
- Fixed bash aliases with line breaks in their value (except in Git Bash), and functions whose names start with a dash, being garbled or lost in the Bash tool's shell
- Fixed bash scripts started from the Bash tool stopping after their first command when `SHELLOPTS` is exported
- Fixed PowerShell hooks not blocking on exit code 2 when the command begins with a type cast, `param`, `using` or an attribute
- Fixed some network requests hanging when a compressed response was cut off or corrupted
- Fixed `sonnet`, `opus` and `haiku` on Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock showing an error mid-session instead of switching to an older model when the newest is not yet available to the account or region
- Fixed the Claude apps gateway not checking every model a request names against `availableModels`, `deniedModels` and `models`; a request that names a blocked model now gets a 400 naming the field
- Fixed `claude auth login` refusing to run where managed settings require a Claude apps gateway; in a terminal it now shows the gateway sign-in
- Fixed `--restricted` sessions uploading files from outside the working directories when a Read allow rule covered them
- Fixed prompts containing invisible characters needing a second Enter to send; plain prompts now send cleaned on the first Enter, and commands still wait for review
- Fixed sub-agents that inherited a parent sub-agent's model moving to the main model when a background job or message woke them
- Fixed a managed `autoMode.allow` list without `"$defaults"` getting the built-in exceptions back from a host app's `--settings`, a first rule added in `/permissions`, or `/auto-mode-setup`
- Fixed cloud sessions and cloud scheduled tasks not being marked as failed when auto mode stopped a turn because the server returned no safety verdict
- Fixed `claude -p` text output sometimes not saying why auto mode stopped a turn when a background agent was still running
- Fixed `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=1` being ignored in sessions started by a host application (such as Claude Desktop) behind a proxy or LLM gateway with experimental betas turned off
- Fixed plugin MCP `headersHelper` scripts receiving a corrupted `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` and server URL when a credential-named environment variable was set to a switch value such as `1`
- Fixed the SDK `register_repo_root` control request not loading the CLAUDE.md of a directory outside the working directory (with `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1`)
- Fixed the Artifact tool showing `?` for artifact database access rules at the `self` level, and not quoting those rules back when it refuses a republish that would drop them
- Fixed `/model <id>` not warning when the model isn't recognized by this version and auto-compact will assume a 200K context window
- Fixed the "hold space to speak" hint using up its three showings in one session, and showing an empty key when push-to-talk is unbound
- Fixed Grep and Glob never returning when the search process is killed at the timeout but does not exit, seen on Windows
- Fixed a rare case where resuming a conversation did not restore its plan, when `/clear` or `/resume` had been run while part of that conversation was still being saved
- Fixed first-run setup dropping words from the security notes and the terminal-setup explanation in narrow terminals
- Fixed the Enterprise survey card taking a typed 1 or 0 after a short pause; a typed answer now needs Enter
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed a message sent while Claude was working being answered after a Stop, once the session's process had been replaced
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed an MCP server's on/off switch sometimes being lost when a session moved to a new machine
- Windows: Fixed the Bash tool losing your aliases and functions in Git Bash when the rc file sets errexit and pipefail and only winpty aliases, or none, are defined
- Improved `/code-review` started from the Code tab in Claude Desktop or on the web: cloud and `claude remote-control` sessions now show the findings card, not a plain-text list
- Improved `/diff` on large repositories: each refresh usually runs one fewer full-repository git command, and refreshes are spaced out when git is slow
- Improved the messages shown when `/ultrareview`, a cloud session or a cloud agent finds no GitHub remote: they now say to create a repository at https://github.com/new, and `/ultrareview` no longer suggests a `gh` command that `gh` rejects
- Improved SSL certificate errors to name the likely causes, among them a server that leaves out an intermediate certificate, and the fix for each
- Changed auto mode so that an `autoMode.allow` list without `"$defaults"` no longer removes the built-in rule on scheduled-task prompts
- Changed server-managed settings for Team and Enterprise logins: settings fetched from Anthropic's API now apply without an approval prompt, and a stored copy that doesn't verify is refused
- [VSCode] Added sign-in to a Claude apps gateway from the chat panel, with no terminal needed
- [VSCode] Changed `ultrathink` to run its turn at `xhigh` effort and show in a rainbow in the chat box, as in the terminal
- [VSCode] Fixed the missing Effort slider, Ultracode switch and model name when the model setting has the `[1m]` tag, such as `opus[1m]`
- [VSCode] Fixed saved `/btw` side-question history being deleted too early while a settings file has errors
- [VSCode] Fixed a conversation coming back in Auto mode after a reload or restart when its plan was approved with "Yes, and manually approve edits"
- [Cloud sessions] Added a form card to cloud sessions, so you can fill in or decline a form an MCP server asks for instead of the request being canceled without you seeing it
- [Cloud sessions] Added a "Catching up…" line that shows while a cloud or Remote Control session you switch back to is still bringing its messages up to date
- [Cloud sessions] Changed network secrets so Enterprise members can add and delete them on their own cloud environments, instead of only viewing them
- [Cloud sessions] Improved the Changes pane for cloud sessions: the note about what the list leaves out is now a badge beside the branch name, not a row above the diff
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed file search in a cloud session's Files pane showing folders as ../.. paths after Claude changed directory; results now show their path from the project's root
- [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude refusing to edit or append to a canvas it made in a Slack channel, from that channel, once the canvas was also shared to another channel or a DM
- [Claude Tag] Fixed untagged replies going unanswered in a Slack Connect thread when both organizations have installed Claude and Slack delivered the reply to the other organization's app
- [Claude Tag] Fixed a cloud scheduled task's live status checklist in Slack staying half-done; a run can now edit the top-level messages it posted during that run
- [Claude Tag] Changed a Slack channel's Respond automatically switch to a "How Claude participates" choice on the channel's Configure page and in Claude Tag admin settings
- [Code Review] Added a findings-by-severity card to the Code Review analytics page, showing the period's total findings, a daily chart stacked by severity, and each severity's count

items.titleRaw: anthropics/claude-code v2.1.311 released
items.contentRaw:
## What's changed

- Added `--hold-idle-file` and `--max-hold-min` to `self-hosted-runner`, to keep an idle session while your host reports processes it left running
- Added a tip for the Explanatory output style, shown when you ask Claude for explanations
- Fixed long freezes at startup and after reading or editing files when a CLAUDE.md file holds a very long list item
- Fixed interrupting Claude not taking effect until a timeout while an MCP server had not answered a resource read or a skill was still downloading
- Fixed standard-context sessions stopping with "Usage credits required for 1M context" when a request ran over 200K tokens; Claude Code now compacts the conversation and continues
- Fixed Write and Edit stalling for up to 5 seconds after they ran, and reporting 0 lines changed, when changing thousands of lines in a file
- Fixed subagents being unable to use MCP tools from servers that finish connecting after the subagent starts
- Fixed Claude seeing stale MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md content right after automatic compaction when those files were edited earlier in the session
- Fixed `claude -p` and SDK sessions saving transcript messages out of order or keeping messages that were taken back
- Fixed `SubagentStop` hooks running about twice a minute for each running subagent instead of once when it finishes
- Fixed the @ file picker ignoring `.ignore`/`.rgignore` negation rules that re-include git-ignored files
- Fixed a subagent's isolated worktree being removed while a background subagent it started was still working in it
- Fixed background agents in auto mode that wait on their own shells starting a new main conversation turn on every wake
- Fixed the Bash tool description claiming the working directory always persists between calls
- Fixed the environment block naming a shell commands don't run in, such as fish when the Bash tool uses zsh
- Fixed `claude mcp add`, `claude mcp remove` and `/mcp` naming the current folder instead of the project entry in `~/.claude.json` that holds a local-scope server when run below a repository root
- Fixed `claude mcp list` and `claude mcp get` showing the error code twice on failed-connection lines (for example `ENOENT: ENOENT: …`)
- Fixed Remote Control sessions staying on "Connecting" for about two minutes when a network proxy blocks a startup request
- Fixed messages that Claude sends to a cloud or Remote Control session appearing as your own message in the Claude mobile apps
- Fixed Claude not being told the cause when a file attached to a message sent over Remote Control or to a cloud session could not be saved because the disk was full, or that a message's attachments past the first 20 were left out
- Fixed WebFetch and WebSearch hanging on a stalled response in Cowork cloud sessions; an unfinished request now fails after 300 seconds
- Fixed a background session that crashed between turns not being restarted while it was attached, pinned, or had a scheduled task or wake-up set
- Fixed the "background service did not respond" error suggesting the disabled `claude daemon restart`; it now suggests `claude daemon stop --any` and says it ends background sessions
- Fixed `claude respawn <id>` starting the background service before reporting that no background session matches the id
- Fixed `/effort` not warning about a prompt cache miss in plan mode when the plan model differs from the session model
- Fixed `/ide` saying the VS Code extension was installed before the install finished or when it failed
- Fixed the Write tool's file preview skipping rows and miscounting hidden lines when a line is wider than the terminal
- Fixed ↑ in an agent's chat tab recalling a message that was still waiting to be delivered, so resending it sent a second copy
- Fixed Cowork cloud sessions losing their connectors and most tools after a restart when a plugin or your settings named an `agent`; Cowork cloud sessions now ignore that setting
- Fixed agent teams sessions showing an empty task list when coming back with `--resume`, `--continue`, `/resume` or `--session-id`, including after `/clear` or a crash, and `/branch` writing to the original session's list
- Fixed pasting text that mentions an image file, such as `! open /tmp/shot.png` or `/review look at /tmp/shot.png`, attaching the image and dropping its path from the prompt
- Fixed the feedback draft card showing its 1/2/0 and Esc shortcuts while the prompt has text, when those keys act on the prompt instead of the card
- Fixed a lone backslash in quotes or brackets, like `"\"` or `(\)`, disappearing from Claude's responses
- Fixed agent teammates compacting their history when `DISABLE_COMPACT` is set
- Fixed the rewind menu offering "Summarize from here" and "Summarize up to here" when `DISABLE_COMPACT` is set
- Fixed a finished `/code-review`, or another skill that runs in a sub-agent, running a second time when a cloud or background session restarts
- Fixed long hidden thinking being cut off as idle on Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS, where the endpoint sends thinking progress updates
- Fixed `/ide` saying it had installed the JetBrains plugin when nothing was installed
- Fixed Claude Pro and Max subscribers being told to ask their admin when their subscription can't be used; the message now points to billing settings
- Fixed the diff pane opening by itself after an edit in wide fullscreen terminals when it had nothing to show
- Fixed `/mcp` showing a remote server as failed after "Clear authentication" when the server works without sign-in
- Fixed `/mcp` showing "authenticated" for a remote server that Claude Code sends no credentials to
- Fixed a `--plugin-dir` folder of plugins loading as one plugin when an empty `.mcp.json` was at its top
- Fixed `/usage` never showing large prompt-cache misses under "What's contributing to your limits usage?"
- Fixed status line links staying plain text in background sessions after you open them from a terminal that supports links
- Fixed the /rewind confirmation saying the conversation "will be forked" when the later messages are removed from the conversation
- Fixed the /rewind warning that wrongly said manual and Bash edits are never affected by a code restore
- Fixed plan approval in screen reader mode sending feedback you had dismissed with Escape
- Fixed Claude Code retrying requests the API marked not to retry, which could hold a turn for minutes or, in unattended retry mode (`CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG`), indefinitely
- Linux: Fixed sandboxed Bash commands failing with `bwrap: Can't create file` when a `--plugin-dir` folder was also an added directory and `permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories` was on
- Self-hosted runner: Fixed a session failing to start when a rate limit (HTTP 429, or a git wrapper that exits 75) blocks an added read-only repository; it now starts without that repository
- Improved startup time for Pro and Max accounts by skipping two network requests on launches within an hour of the last check
- Improved `/teleport` and `claude --teleport` to warn when a compacted cloud session loads from its last compaction, so the messages it summarized aren't in the local copy
- Improved the messages shown when a background session's process exits: they no longer promise a restart that isn't coming, and they say how to resume the session
- Improved artifacts with several views: Claude now routes each view on the link's `#name` and no longer says the address bar stays the same as you switch views
- Improved shell commands that reach their timeout: the result now shows the output so far and says the command is still running in the background
- Improved compaction: when the model's reply has no summary in it, Claude Code now usually asks for the summary once more before it replaces the conversation
- Improved the Artifact tool's choice between a page and a document: explainers and visual or interactive work become artifact pages; documents are for writing people keep editing or pass around
- Improved startup time for launches whose only arguments are options and their values, such as `claude --model opus`
- Improved the "Connection dropped" API error: it now says where to look first (the proxy or gateway in use, else VPN or firewall; Anthropic API only, Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry are unchanged)
- Improved screen reader mode: deleting a rule in /permissions says "Deleted allow rule …" right away
- Improved the message shown when a pasted sign-in code is refused: it now says the code may have expired or been used, and to sign in again
- Improved Slack connector sends: Claude now checks a channel's topic for posting rules before messaging a channel you didn't name
- Improved screen reader mode: Claude's questions are listed as "Questions: Color (answered), Pages", without arrows or symbols
- Changed `ultrathink` in the interactive terminal to run its turn at xhigh effort on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 through Anthropic's API; typed while Claude is working, it raises the rest of that turn
- Changed the `ultrathink` rainbow to appear only where the keyword can raise effort, and not when the word is quoted or part of a file path
- Changed Ctrl+D in agent view to match the prompt: on an empty input, pressing it twice exits
- Changed `--output-format json` and `stream-json` output to write DEL, C1 control and Unicode format characters inside strings as `\uXXXX` escapes; parsed values are unchanged
- Changed model names and IDs to drop the `[1m]` suffix and its label on models where the suffix has no effect; the suffix is still accepted
- Changed startup warnings about permission rules in settings files to show once per user until the rule changes
- Changed `/code-review` to tell Claude to put the effort level first and use max only when asked
- Changed `DISABLE_COMPACT` in settings files and in a mod's `$.env.set` so they can only turn compaction off, not back on
- Changed Claude Code on Bedrock, Mantle, Vertex, and Foundry to load model settings from a signed file on downloads.claude.ai; set CLAUDE_CODE_MODEL_CATALOG=off to turn this off
- Changed sessions that set `CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS` with feature-flag fetching off to reuse a claude.ai skills list up to 10 minutes old that another session on the machine fetched
- Changed clicks on scrollbar arrows and bars in fullscreen lists to act when the mouse button is released, so moving off the scrollbar before letting go cancels the click
- Changed `claude purge` to say it deletes data only on this computer, not anything stored by Anthropic
- [VSCode] Added syntax coloring to code blocks in Claude's replies, in light, dark and high contrast dark themes
- [VSCode] Added a "Running UserPromptSubmit hooks" spinner status and screen reader announcement for slow UserPromptSubmit hooks
- [VSCode] Fixed custom skills and custom slash commands sent from the VS Code or JetBrains panel leaving out the open file or selected lines that ordinary messages include (anthropics/claude-code#102799)
- [VSCode] Fixed the extension host freezing while the login shell ran its start-up files to read PATH on macOS and Linux
- [VSCode] Fixed clicking an image in a tool result, or closing its preview, also opening the result's text in an editor tab
- [VSCode] Fixed voice dictation continuing to record after a message was sent with the Send button; sending now stops dictation first, as pressing Enter already did
- [VSCode] Changed the extension to start Claude Code sessions with `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` set while VS Code's telemetry setting is off, so they send no usage metrics or error reports and fetch no feature flags
- [VSCode] Changed the session list side bar to load Web sessions when the Web tab is first opened, not at startup
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed routines in Anthropic-hosted environments staying locked after their owner left the organization and rejoined; the owner can now turn them back on
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed a failed routine API token delete or regenerate showing nothing if the edit dialog had already closed; it now shows an error toast
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed cloud environment dialogs, including the admin dialog, accepting duplicate names; they now refuse a name another listed environment already has
- [Claude Tag] Added a Skills view to Claude Tag analytics showing how often Claude runs each attached skill in Slack channels and which go unused, with Usage links in admin settings
- [Claude Tag] Improved Claude Tag routines that run in a new session: a run with nothing to report can now end without posting a throwaway message to the channel
- [Claude Tag] Changed Claude Tag admin settings to show a lock instead of # for private Slack channels that your own Slack account can see
- [Code Review] Improved Code Review's check run to say no further automatic review will start when the model still can't analyze a change on the automatic retry
- [Code Review] Improved Code Review reliability: a review whose session fails to start because of a transient server fault is now retried once automatically, and its check run says so

- Improved screen reader mode: Claude's questions are listed as "Questions: Color (answered), Pages", without arrows or symbols
- Changed `ultrathink` in the interactive terminal to run its turn at xhigh effort on Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Fable 5.1 through Anthropic's API; typed while Claude is working, it raises the rest of that turn
- Changed the `ultrathink` rainbow to appear only where the keyword can raise effort, and not when the word is quoted or part of a file path
- Changed Ctrl+D in agent view to match the prompt: on an empty input, pressing it twice exits
- Changed `--output-format json` and `stream-json` output to write DEL, C1 control and Unicode format characters inside strings as `\uXXXX` escapes; parsed values are unchanged
- Changed model names and IDs to drop the `[1m]` suffix and its label on models where the suffix has no effect; the suffix is still accepted
- Changed startup warnings about permission rules in settings files to show once per user until the rule changes
- Changed `/code-review` to tell Claude to put the effort level first and use max only when asked
- Changed `DISABLE_COMPACT` in settings files and in a mod's `$.env.set` so they can only turn compaction off, not back on
- Changed Claude Code on Bedrock, Mantle, Vertex, and Foundry to load model settings from a signed file on downloads.claude.ai; set CLAUDE_CODE_MODEL_CATALOG=off to turn this off
- Changed sessions that set `CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS` with feature-flag fetching off to reuse a claude.ai skills list up to 10 minutes old that another session on the machine fetched
- Changed clicks on scrollbar arrows and bars in fullscreen lists to act when the mouse button is released, so moving off the scrollbar before letting go cancels the click
- Changed `claude purge` to say it deletes data only on this computer, not anything stored by Anthropic
- [VSCode] Added syntax coloring to code blocks in Claude's replies, in light, dark and high contrast dark themes
- [VSCode] Added a "Running UserPromptSubmit hooks" spinner status and screen reader announcement for slow UserPromptSubmit hooks
- [VSCode] Fixed custom skills and custom slash commands sent from the VS Code or JetBrains panel leaving out the open file or selected lines that ordinary messages include (anthropics/claude-code#102799)
- [VSCode] Fixed the extension host freezing while the login shell ran its start-up files to read PATH on macOS and Linux
- [VSCode] Fixed clicking an image in a tool result, or closing its preview, also opening the result's text in an editor tab
- [VSCode] Fixed voice dictation continuing to record after a message was sent with the Send button; sending now stops dictation first, as pressing Enter already did
- [VSCode] Changed the extension to start Claude Code sessions with `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` set while VS Code's telemetry setting is off, so they send no usage metrics or error reports and fetch no feature flags
- [VSCode] Changed the session list side bar to load Web sessions when the Web tab is first opened, not at startup
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed routines in Anthropic-hosted environments staying locked after their owner left the organization and rejoined; the owner can now turn them back on
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed a failed routine API token delete or regenerate showing nothing if the edit dialog had already closed; it now shows an error toast
- [Cloud sessions] Fixed cloud environment dialogs, including the admin dialog, accepting duplicate names; they now refuse a name another listed environment already has
- [Claude Tag] Added a Skills view to Claude Tag analytics showing how often Claude runs each attached skill in Slack channels and which go unused, with Usage links in admin settings
- [Claude Tag] Improved Claude Tag routines that run in a new session: a run with nothing to report can now end without posting a throwaway message to the channel
- [Claude Tag] Changed Claude Tag admin settings to show a lock instead of # for private Slack channels that your own Slack account can see
- [Code Review] Improved Code Review's check run to say no further automatic review will start when the model still can't analyze a change on the automatic retry
- [Code Review] Improved Code Review reliability: a review whose session fails to start because of a transient server fault is now retried once automatically, and its check run says so

Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union. #### Key Features Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices: - **~1T total / ~52B active parameters**: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert. - **1M context length**, for long-context workloads. - **Multimodal input**: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios. - **Instruct and Reasoning functionalities** with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request. Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities: - **Reasoning Mode**: three reasoning efforts — `low`, `medium`, `high` (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run. - **Vision**: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights. - **Multilingual**: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union. - **System Prompt**: strong adherence and support for system prompts. - **Agentic**: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement. - **Cybersecurity**: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests. - **Large Context Window**: supports a 1M context window. The model is released under the [**Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License**](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B/blob/main/LICENSE): a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use — operating a Model-as-a-Service business requires a separate commercial license with Mistral. #### Recommended Settings - **Reasoning Effort**: - `'low'` / `'medium'` / `'high'` — default is `'high'`. - Use `reasoning_effort="high"` for complex prompts and agentic usage, `'low'` for fast chat replies and `'medium'` for day to day usage. - **Sampling**: for all reasoning efforts, we recommend the following sampling parameters: - `temperature=1.0` - `top_p=0.95` - **System Prompt**: define a clear environment and use case, including guidance on how to effectively leverage tools in agentic systems. - **Tools**: keep the set of tools well-defined and limit their number to the minimum required for the use case. - **Context**: the checkpoint supports a 1M context window. ## Breaking changes * 🚨 Separate EP logic into its own file (#49679) by @3outeille ## Quantization FP8 quantized models can now be used for adapter training (such as LoRA with PEFT). Backward passes were added to the dense and grouped FP8 matmuls, and `is_trainable` is now `True`. Backward also dequantizes experts in chunks and skips autograd at inference, which cuts peak memory in the MoE layer backward from about 28.9 GiB to 2.8 GiB at 8k tokens. items.contentRaw: # Release v5.21.0 ## New Model additions ### MiniCPM-OCR MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/minicpm_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) * Feat test (#49920) by @guarin in [#49920](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49920) ### Flint Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/flint) * Add Flint model support. (#49824) by @lovishmadaan in [#49824](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49824) ### UltraVBert UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The `max_image_tiles` setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultravbert) * Add UltraVBERT (#49685) by @athrael-soju in [#49685](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49685) ### Gradium Phonon TTS Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. A causal transformer reads a voice prompt and the text, then emits one continuous 32-dimensional audio latent per step at 12.5 Hz through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when the utterance ends. The latents are decoded to 24 kHz audio by a Pocket TTS audio tokenizer. Unlike Pocket TTS, voice conditioning uses 512-dimensional latents from a separate, unreleased speaker codec, so voices come as precomputed latents and cannot be cloned from a recording. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/gradium_phonon_tts) * Add GradiumPhononTTS (#49791) by @eustlb in [#49791](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49791) ### Pocket TTS Pocket TTS is Kyutai's 100M-parameter text-to-speech model, built as a Continuous Audio Language Model that runs faster than real time on CPU. A causal transformer emits one continuous audio latent per frame (12.5 Hz) through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when to stop. A Mimi-based audio tokenizer encodes voice prompts and decodes the generated latents to 24 kHz audio. Two flow heads are released, Lagrangian self-distillation (default) and drifting, and voices can be cloned from a recording, passed as precomputed latents, or loaded from cached KV states. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (the Continuous Audio Language Models paper, arXiv 2509.06926). It is the only paper the documentation links, and it describes the architecture family Pocket TTS belongs to. The docs do not cite a separate Pocket TTS technical report.) | [Blog Post](NONE. The documentation links no official blog post. It points only to the original code repository at https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts.) * add PocketTTS (#49589) by @eustlb in [#49589](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49589) ### Pocket TTS Audio Tokenizer The Pocket TTS audio tokenizer is the codec used by Pocket TTS. It has Mimi's architecture (SEANet convolutions plus a small causal transformer on each side), but its residual vector quantizer is replaced by a continuous 32-dimensional bottleneck, the VAE-GAN from Continuous Audio Language Models. It converts 24 kHz audio into latents at 12.5 Hz and decodes them back to audio. It serves as the `audio_tokenizer` of `PocketTTSProcessor`, encoding voice prompts and decoding generated latents, and its encoder and decoder can also be loaded on their own. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts_audio_tokenizer) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (Continuous Audio Language Models, whose VAE-GAN this tokenizer uses; arxiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06926)) * add PocketTTSAudioTokenizer (#49588) by @eustlb in [#49588](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49588) ## Breaking changes Fixed Gemma4 processor imports (the Gemma4, Gemma4 unified and EmbeddingGemma2 processors) so `from transformers import *` no longer fails in environments that have `PIL` but not `torch`; no user action is needed. * :rotating_light: Fix gemma4 cross imports resulting in import failing without `torch` but with `PIL` (#49748) by @Sai-Suraj-27 Added an `"fp8"` backend to `QuantizedCache`, alongside `quanto` and `hqq`, that stores KV states in `torch.float8_e4m3fn` with a single scale per tensor; enable it with `cache_implementation="quantized"` and `cache_config={"backend": "fp8"}`. * 🚨Add an FP8 backend to `QuantizedCache` (#48677) by @jiqing-feng Tensor parallelism now has a dedicated embedding style, shards every model's input embeddings by default, and supports widths that aren't divisible by the TP size, so `ColwiseParallel` and `RowwiseParallel` now apply only to linear layers; custom TP plans that applied them to embeddings must switch to the new embedding style. * 🚨 TP: give embeddings their own style, shard input embeddings by default, and shard widths that don't divide by the TP size (#49570) by @IlyasMoutawwakil Every MoE TP and EP plan now shards its experts, so models no longer keep all experts on every rank, and a new `test_moe_parallel_plans_shard_experts` test enforces this; custom or downstream MoE parallel plans must add expert sharding to pass it and to avoid wasted memory. * 🚨 MoE: shard the experts in every TP/EP plan, and test for it (#49206) by @IlyasMoutawwakil ## Cache This release improves cache handling across the library. Flash Attention now works with static caches, BLOOM no longer crashes with static cache or compiled generate, chunked prefill supports cache continuation, and the Qwen4-Exp indexer's position history stays aligned with its cached keys. Linear-attention caches also gain new getters (`is_recording_past`, `get_recurrent_state`, conv-state access) that stop exposing cache internals and prepare for paged-c * [FA] Fix FA with static cache (#49998) by @Cyrilvallez in [#49998] * [docs] CB cache behavior (#49025) by @stevhliu in [#49025] * [CB] Reduce warmup time by not computing attention over full cache (#49853) by @remi-or in [#49853] * Fix Qwen4-Exp indexer position cache lifecycle (#49840) by @taking-lying-flat in [#49840] * [Cache] Linear attn cache: use new getters (#49375) by @remi-or in [#49375] * [Cache] Get conv states (#49309) by @remi-or in [#49309] * [Cache] Add get_recurrent_state (#49306) by @remi-or in [#49306] * [Cache] Add is_recording_past (#49305) by @remi-or in [#49305] * Fix BLOOM crash with static cache / compiled generate (#49481) by @kaixuanliu in [#49481] * Allow Cache continuation for chunked prefill (#49662) by @Cyrilvallez in [#49662] ## Vision Vision image processors now composite PNG transparency onto white instead of exposing black pixels, and `background_color` is preserved correctly across the DeepSeek-VL and Janus processors. Model fixes cover SmolVLM's `inputs_merger` when image tokens aren't a multiple of the patch size, HunYuan-VL image assignment during batched beam search, and Ernie4.5-VL-MoE expert sharding under TP/EP. The DETR * Composite transparency in shared RGB conversion and image processors (#49079) by @Nikhi00718 in [#49079] * [Fetcher] Fix missing test deps for dynamically-resolved image processors (#49826) by @ydshieh in [#49826] * fix(vision): Route the DETR conversion scripts through from_pretrained (#49830) by @harshaljanjani in [#49830] * Fix background_color handling across DeepSeek-VL and Janus image processors (#49767) by @tritsystem in [#49767] * Move the MI300 docker image to ROCm 10.1 and update test expectations (#49460) by @Abdennacer-Badaoui in [#49460] * docs: fix 'allows to' grammar in Vision Encoder Decoder docs (#48730) by @mrchatam in [#48730] * Fix SSH runner: add /opt/venv/bin to PATH for Python 3.11 images (#49759) by @ydshieh in [#49759] * Fix SmolVLM inputs_merger when image tokens are not a multiple of patch_size (#49725) by @albertvillanova in [#49725] * Ernie4.5-VL-MoE: shard the text and vision experts under TP and EP (#49462) by @IlyasMoutawwakil in [#49462] * Fix HunYuan-VL image assignment during batched generation (#49557) by @Arnav66692 in [#49557] ## Generation This release fixes a range of generation bugs: BLOOM crashes with static cache or compiled generate, `generate` dropping the type of dict-like inputs such as `ModelOutput`, and incorrect image assignment or placeholder handling in batched or beam-search generation for HunYuan-VL and Idefics2/3. It also fixes Qwen3-Omni audio generation mode handling, SAM mask-generation multi-zoom crops, empty frame s * fix: prevent empty frame sampling for short videos (#49908) by @BlazeSR10hawk in [#49908] * Fix Windows path separators breaking relative imports of Hub custom-generate modules (#48951) by @dltsum in [#48951] * Fix multi-zoom crops in the SAM mask-generation pipeline and related bugs (Fixes #35530) (#49689) by @stlukyanenko in [#49689] * update speculative decoding docs (#49697) by @merveenoyan in [#49697] * fix idefics3 generation issues (#49738) by @molbap in [#49738] * fix tests for generation (#49740) by @molbap in [#49740] * Fix inputs dict casting in `generate` (#49731) by @Cyrilvallez in [#49731] * [fix][Qwen3-Omni] Respect generation_mode in audio generation (#49505) by @Sunt-ing in [#49505] ## Parallelization This release extends parallelism support and fixes several related bugs. It adds a tensor-parallel plan for Nemotron and makes Ernie4.5-VL-MoE shard its text and vision experts under TP and EP. release.body: # Release v5.21.0 ## New Model additions ### MiniCPM-OCR MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/minicpm_ocr) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.18154) * Feat test (#49920) by @guarin in [#49920](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49920) ### Flint Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/flint) * Add Flint model support. (#49824) by @lovishmadaan in [#49824](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49824) ### UltraVBert UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The `max_image_tiles` setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/ultravbert) * Add UltraVBERT (#49685) by @athrael-soju in [#49685](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49685) ### Gradium Phonon TTS Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. A causal transformer reads a voice prompt and the text, then emits one continuous 32-dimensional audio latent per step at 12.5 Hz through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when the utterance ends. The latents are decoded to 24 kHz audio by a Pocket TTS audio tokenizer. Unlike Pocket TTS, voice conditioning uses 512-dimensional latents from a separate, unreleased speaker codec, so voices come as precomputed latents and cannot be cloned from a recording. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/gradium_phonon_tts) * Add GradiumPhononTTS (#49791) by @eustlb in [#49791](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49791) ### Pocket TTS Pocket TTS is Kyutai's 100M-parameter text-to-speech model, built as a Continuous Audio Language Model that runs faster than real time on CPU. A causal transformer emits one continuous audio latent per frame (12.5 Hz) through a one-step flow head, and an end-of-speech head decides when to stop. A Mimi-based audio tokenizer encodes voice prompts and decodes the generated latents to 24 kHz audio. Two flow heads are released, Lagrangian self-distillation (default) and drifting, and voices can be cloned from a recording, passed as precomputed latents, or loaded from cached KV states. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (the Continuous Audio Language Models paper, arXiv 2509.06926). It is the only paper the documentation links, and it describes the architecture family Pocket TTS belongs to. The docs do not cite a separate Pocket TTS technical report.) | [Blog Post](NONE. The documentation links no official blog post. It points only to the original code repository at https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts.) * add PocketTTS (#49589) by @eustlb in [#49589](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49589) ### Pocket TTS Audio Tokenizer The Pocket TTS audio tokenizer is the codec used by Pocket TTS. It has Mimi's architecture (SEANet convolutions plus a small causal transformer on each side), but its residual vector quantizer is replaced by a continuous 32-dimensional bottleneck, the VAE-GAN from Continuous Audio Language Models. It converts 24 kHz audio into latents at 12.5 Hz and decodes them back to audio. It serves as the `audio_tokenizer` of `PocketTTSProcessor`, encoding voice prompts and decoding generated latents, and its encoder and decoder can also be loaded on their own. **Links:** [Documentation](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/pocket_tts_audio_tokenizer) | [Paper](https://huggingface.co/papers/2509.06926 (Continuous Audio Language Models, whose VAE-GAN this tokenizer uses; arxiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06926)) * add PocketTTSAudioTokenizer (#49588) by @eustlb in [#49588](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/49588) ## Breaking changes Fixed Gemma4 processor imports (the Gemma4, Gemma4 unified and EmbeddingGemma2 processors) so `from transformers import *` no longer fails in environments that have `PIL` but not `torch`; no user action is needed. * :rotating_light: Fix gemma4 cross imports resulting in import failing without `torch` but with `PIL` (#49748) by @Sai-Suraj-27 Added an `"fp8"` backend to `QuantizedCache`, alongside `quanto` and `hqq`, that stores KV states in `torch.float8_e4m3fn` with a single scale per tensor; enable it with `cache_implementation="quantized"` and `cache_config={"backend": "fp8"}`. * 🚨Add an FP8 backend to `QuantizedCache` (#48677) by @jiqing-feng Tensor parallelism now has a dedicated embedding style, shards every model's input embeddings by default, and supports widths that aren't divisible by the TP size, so `ColwiseParallel` and `RowwiseParallel` now apply only to linear layers; Flash Attention now works with static caches, BLOOM no longer crashes with static cache or compiled generate, chunked prefill supports cache continuation, and the Qwen4-Exp indexer's position history stays aligned with its cached keys. items.titleRaw: ollama/ollama v0.40.12 released
items.contentRaw:
## Liquid AI LFM3

[LFM3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3) is Liquid AI's new family of small models built for local agents, tool calling, and structured output, on Liquid's new tri-hybrid architecture. The family includes:

- [lfm3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3): a 1.7B text model with a 256K-token context window
- [lfm3-vl](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-vl): adds image understanding
- [lfm3-audio](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-audio): speech recognition, translation, and text-to-speech in 18 languages
- [lfm3-omni](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-omni): text, images, and audio in one model

```sh
ollama run lfm3
```

## d1 decision models

Liquid AI's d1 models now come in a 2B size, built on LFM3. [d1](https://ollama.com/library/d1) makes decisions about text and images, and [d1-omni](https://ollama.com/library/d1-omni) adds audio.

```sh
ollama run d1:2b "I was charged twice for order 4417." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

Note: lfm3 and d1 2b are supported on Apple hardware in this release.  Support for Linux/Windows coming soon.

## What's Changed
- Faster prompt processing on Apple silicon for Gemma 4, Flint and Laguna models
- Speculative decoding now supports DFlash2 draft models on MLX
- Gemma 4 keeps more detail in small images
- `ollama launch` now works with OpenCode v2
- Fixed tool-only assistant turns from Kimi CLI
- Updated MLX and llama.cpp

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.11...v0.40.12

items.titleRaw: ollama/ollama v0.40.11 released
items.contentRaw:
## Speech

Ollama can now generate [speech](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech) on macOS. `ollama run` plays text or a chat model's reply aloud as the audio is generated, and apps can stream audio through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint.

```sh
ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama."
```

## d3 decision models

[d3](https://ollama.com/library/d3) brings vLLM Semantic Router's decision models to Ollama. Give a model text, structured state, or an image, and ask it to classify, answer yes or no, or score options with probabilities. The family includes 2B, 4B, 9B, and 27B sizes.

```sh
ollama run d3 "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
```

items.contentRaw:
AgentState to solve a problem I kept running into: managing state for multi-agent AI systems is surprisingly hard. When you have multiple AI agents that need to coordinate, persist their state, and query each other's status, you typically end up with a mess of Redis/Postgres setups, custom queuing, and manual synchronization code.

The whole thing is ~3MB, written in Rust for performance and safety, runs in Docker, and handles 1000+ ops/sec. I've been running it in production for AI workflows and it's been rock solid.

items.titleRaw: Show HN: ML Blocks – Deploy multimodal AI workflows without code
items.contentRaw:
Hey everyone,

ML Blocks is a node-based workflow builder to create multi-modal AI workflows without writing any code.

You connect blocks that call various visual models like GPT4v, Segment Anything, Dino etc. along with basic image processing blocks like resize, invert color, blur, crop, and several others.

The idea is to make it easier to deploy multi-step image processing workflows, without needing to spin up endless custom OpenCV cloud functions to glue together AI models. Usually, even if you're using cloud inference servers like Replicate, you still need to write your own image processing code to pre and post-process images in your pipeline. When you're trying to move fast, that's just unnecessary overhead.

With ML Blocks, you can build a workflow and deploy the whole thing as a single API. AFAIK, ML Blocks is the only end-to-end workflow builder built specifically for image processing.

If you're curious, our models run on Replicate, HuggingFace & Modal Labs cloud GPUs and we use React Flow for the node UX.
